definitions.explanation: The act of competing against or standing in opposition to someone or something. Implies actively matching or countering an opposing force.

examples.japanese: {大手|おおて}{企業|きぎょう}に{対抗|たいこう}する。
examples.english: To compete against a major corporation.

examples.japanese: {値下|ねさ}げに{対抗|たいこう}して、うちも{価格|かかく}を{下|さ}げた。
examples.english: In response to their price cut, we also lowered our prices.

examples.japanese: {住民|じゅうみん}たちは{再開発|さいかいはつ}{計画|けいかく}に{対抗|たいこう}するために{署名|しょめい}{活動|かつどう}を{始|はじ}めた。
examples.english: The residents started a petition drive to oppose the redevelopment plan.

notes:
USAGE:
{対抗|たいこう} functions as a する verb ({対抗|たいこう}する) and also appears frequently as a modifier: {対抗|たいこう}～ (counter-~, rival ~). The pattern ～に{対抗|たいこう}する (to compete against ~, to counter ~) is very common.

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {対決|たいけつ}: showdown, confrontation (more direct and climactic)
- {対立|たいりつ}: opposition, conflict (emphasis on the state of being opposed)
- {競争|きょうそう}: competition (neutral, ongoing rivalry)

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- ～に{対抗|たいこう}する: to compete against ~, to counter ~
- {対抗|たいこう}{措置|そち}: countermeasure
- {対抗|たいこう}{馬|ば}: rival horse, strong contender
- {対抗|たいこう}{意識|いしき}: sense of rivalry
- {対抗|たいこう}{戦|せん}: rivalry match
